summary.plain: Super-Kamiokande searched 956.2 days of gadolinium-loaded data for the diffuse supernova neutrino background, the cumulative neutrino flux from all past supernovae. No significant excess over background predictions was found, and the paper sets 90% confidence upper limits on the flux; it says it updated the world's most stringent limits in the 9.29-17.29 MeV energy region.
summary.technical: DSNB search using 552.2 days of SK-VI (0.01% Gd) and 404.0 days of SK-VII (0.03% Gd) data through September 2023, with two new machine-learning neutron-detection algorithms with Gd, an improved atmospheric-background reduction technique and two parallel statistical approaches. No significant excess over background predictions was found in the spectrum-independent analysis, and 90% C.L. upper limits on the astrophysical electron anti-neutrino flux (neutrino energies beyond 9.3 MeV) were set. A spectral fit exhibited a ~1.2σ disagreement with the null DSNB hypothesis, comparable to a previous result from 5823 days of all SK pure-water phases.

title: Search for Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background with 956.2 days of Super-Kamiokande Gadolinium Dataset
why_it_matters: The paper describes the diffuse supernova neutrino background as the cumulative neutrino flux from all past supernovae in the Universe, and says the magnitude and shape of that flux provide unique information about the cosmic history of massive star formation.
